description: Provider-neutral migration ledger for the immutable portable tenant baseline set. Declares the canonical apply order, the SHA-256 of every artifact, the apply principal and the control-plane role-bootstrap dependency.

ledger_store.note: The table in the tenant database is the source of truth for what a given database actually received. This manifest is the source of truth for what it should have received. Any disagreement is drift.

apply_principal.note: The runner connects as the non-superuser app_migration login and applies every step under SET ROLE app_owner, so app_migration owns no object.

reapply_semantics.note: A step already recorded with a matching SHA-256 is skipped and the run exits successfully. The baseline SQL is not internally idempotent, so re-executing it would fail; the runner must skip rather than re-run. Any disagreement between manifest, artifact file and ledger row is a hard failure instead.

down_migrations.note: The operations contract keeps reversal as an explicit break-glass action outside this ledger. No down step is declared, generated or accepted.

role_bootstrap.note: Roles are cluster-level objects and are not carried by pg_dump. A restore target must be prepared with this bootstrap before the dump is restored; the harness never uses pg_dumpall --roles-only, which would move credentials between clusters.

ledger_bootstrap.note: Creates the app_ledger store itself, so it cannot be recorded as a step in that store.

restore_procedure.dump: pg_dump --format=custom --role=app_owner, run as the non-superuser app_migration login
restore_procedure.restore: pg_restore --exit-on-error --role=app_owner into a target prepared with the role bootstrap; pg_dumpall --roles-only is never used
restore_procedure.note: A restore target needs a temporary, explicitly closed window so the AI SQL guard can be handed back to app_ai_runner and re-grant its own ACL. Without it pg_restore silently leaves the guard executable by PUBLIC and without its app_system grant, because a failed GRANT is a warning rather than an error.

steps.description: Portable business tables, identities, constraints, indexes and the seven final views.
Canonical users, provider identity mapping, transaction-local actor context, grants and RLS.
Portable stored functions, business triggers and the SELECT-only AI SQL guard.
